fact: Uganda's PPDA says the e-GP system, introduced in 2021, is an online platform managing public procurement, and by 2025 its deployment had expanded to 36 procuring and disposing entities.

Uganda's PPDA says e-GP automates the entire procurement cycle from planning, bid advertisement and submission to contract award, invoicing and payment processing, though deployed in 36 entities as of 2025 with a national rollout planned for 1 July 2026.

The Ministry of Finance and PPDA rolled out eGP 2.0 to another 100 public entities on 20 July 2026, bringing the total using the platform to 136, and entities already migrated may not advertise tenders in newspapers (Daily Monitor, citing PPDA and the Acting Accountant General).

The Acting Accountant General said under eGP 2.0 suppliers submit bids, receive notifications and sign contracts electronically, with registration mandatory for firms seeking government business and all 441 procuring entities to migrate by 2029.
PPDA Executive Director Benson Turamye says Uganda already has an Electronic Government Procurement system, run end to end by 36 of more than 400 procurement entities.
Turamye says the 36 entities running EGP have done more than 38,000 contracts on it, with a target of 113 entities by June 2026.
The Ministry of Finance's procurement commissioner states Uganda's home-grown e-GP system was piloted in 5 procuring entities in 2020 and rolled out in 2021, with 36 entities enrolled in May 2025.
The article says Uganda rolled out the e-GP system on 1 July 2021 in 12 pilot entities and that 36 entities were enrolled by March 2024.
The article describes e-GP as using ICT for end-to-end procurement planning, bidding, evaluation, award, contract management, invoicing and payment to providers.
